title: Heterogeneous Hybrid Quantization: Deployment Guidelines and Eval Integration
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Summary:
This document describes operational guidelines for deploying heterogeneous hybrid quantization configurations across Redwood Inference environments (hosted, dedicated, private). It covers required pre-deployment evaluations with the eval-harness, prompt-set sensitivity checks, rollout and canary policies, runtime guardrails to prevent quality regressions, and a regression-triage fast path when quant-related anomalies are detected. The goal is to enable cost-effective quant usage without compromising production-quality SLOs for latency and response fidelity.

Why heterogeneous hybrid quantization?
- Many production workloads contain diverse request profiles (short prompts, long-context conversations, code generation). Using the same quant profile everywhere leads to suboptimal cost/quality tradeoffs.
- Heterogeneous hybrid quantization lets us:
  - Use mixed-precision kernels per-layer or per-device (e.g., int4 KV-cache, fp16 attention heads)
  - Assign traffic by policy (route latency-sensitive traffic to higher-precision pools)
  - Run CPU-bound embeddings with lower precision while keeping generation layers in higher precision

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to models in the Redwood catalog that have a verified quantization artifact (quant profile) and a signed acceptance report from Model Onboarding.
- Target environments: hosted Redwood API, Dedicated pools, Redwood Private (VPC).
- Assumes eval-harness and prompt-set bank are available and up-to-date for target workload slices.

Terminology:
- Quant profile: the YAML/JSON artifact describing per-layer precision and kernel mapping.
- Hybrid quant: mixture of precisions across layers (e.g., int4 for KV, fp16 for attention).
- Heterogeneous deployment: different hosts/nodes serve different quant profiles or precisions simultaneously.

Compatibility matrix (example):
| Model family | Kernel support | Preferred hardware | Minimum SLO target (p95 latency) | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| rwinf-llama-2-70b | fused-int4 + fp16 fallback | A100/A800 | 450ms | Use KV-cache int4; avoid int4 attention on short-context spikes |
| rwinf-progressive-13b | int8 dynamic | T4/GPU-optimized CPU | 120ms | Good for embeddings + short generation |

Onboarding checklist (required before any production routing):
1) Quant profile certification: run quantized accuracy tests (eval-harness) against the production prompt-set slices. Acceptance thresholds:
   - Per-slice accuracy delta <= 1.5% absolute OR model-specific metric tolerance from onboarding doc.
   - Response-stability-index (RSI) drop <= 0.03 from fp16 baseline.
2) Throughput & latency verification: synthetic serving simulation using eval-harness profiles:
   - p50/p95 latency within 10% of baseline for targeted request class; p99 must be evaluated and documented.
   - Token generation throughput measured on target hardware exceeds minimal throughput: see table below.
3) Safety & guardrail run: run safety probes and adversarial prompt set (from prompt-sets-and-benchmarks) and ensure no new high-severity safety failures.
4) Regression runbook: prepare a rollback artifact and automated bisect config (see Regression triage section).

Acceptance table for promotion:
- Unit: per-model-per-slice
- Required artifacts: quant-profile.yaml, eval-report.md, perf-snapshot.json, rollback-artifact.tar

Quant config examples (YAML snippet):
---
model: rwinf-llama-2-70b
profile_name: hybrid-kv-int4-fp16-attn
version: 2026-01-10
mapping:
  - layer_range: [0, 8]
    precision: fp16
    kernel: fused_fp16_attn
  - layer_range: [9, 64]
    precision: int4_kv
    kernel: kv_int4_opt
fallback_policy: "fp16-on-oom"
optimize_for: "latency"
---

Eval-harness integration steps:
1) Create a promotion job in eval-mesh: tag the quant artifact and target slices.
2) Run distributional stability evals: sample from production-fingerprint and run 1000 seeds for stochastic variance budgeting.
3) Run throughput-fidelity sweep: sweep batch sizes [1,4,8], context lengths {64,512,2048}, and record token_latency_p50/p95/p99 and quantized_q_error.
4) If the quantized_q_error exceeds thresholds for any critical slice, mark the artifact as FAIL and attach failure traces.

Routing and policy recommendations:
- Policy rules (examples):
  - route.latency_sensitive == true -> send to fp16-pool or high-precision hybrid nodes
  - route.long_context == true and route.cost_sensitive == true -> send to kv-int4 pool with prefix-caching enabled
- Canary rollout: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% with at least 24 hours between each step and automated metric gates.

Metric gates (automated checks before each expansion):
- latency.p95 <= baseline.p95 * 1.12
- quality.mean_score_drop <= 0.015 (model-specific eval metric)
- safety.high_sev_incidents == 0 (from safety probe)
- error_rate <= baseline_error_rate * 1.15

Runtime guardrails and observability (what to monitor):
- Quantization-specific metrics to export from redwood-serving-runtime:
  - quant_quant_error_by_slice (gauge)
  - quant_memory_savings_percent (gauge)
  - kernel_fallback_count (counter)
  - kv_cache_precision_mismatch_rate (counter)
- Core SLOs to verify:
  - token_latency_p50/p95/p99 per-route
  - response_stability_index (RSI) per-slice
  - quality_regression_alerts (boolean per-deployment)
- Dashboards to create:
  - "Quant Deployment Health" (per-model, per-region): shows quant_quant_error_by_slice, p95 latency, kernel_fallback_count, and cost-per-token delta.
  - "Quant Canary Summary": shows canary cohort metrics vs baseline with statistical significance test results.

Automatic mitigation actions (examples):
1) If kernel_fallback_count > 1000 in 10m window -> trigger immediate rollback to previous quant artifact and alert oncall.
2) If RSI drop > 0.04 on critical slice -> throttle quantized pool and route traffic to dedicated fp16 pool with a 5-minute exponential backoff.
3) If quant_memory_savings_percent spikes unexpectedly (possible encoding error) -> disable prefix caching on quantized nodes and create incident for triage.

Regression triage fast path (when a quant deployment causes quality regressions):
1) Freeze rollout and switch to rollback artifact.
2) Launch automated bisect: the bisect tool will subdivide by quant-profile dimension (layer ranges, kernel variant, rounding scheme) instead of full model checkpoints.
3) Run targeted eval slices from the failing cohort with increased seed coverage (x5) to reduce stochastic noise.
4) If bisect points to kernel variant -> reproduce locally with profiler and capture kernel traces (trace ids: TRC-QUANT-<timestamp>).
5) If bisect point is non-deterministic, escalate to Research/Applied ML for stability experiments and schedule a canary with stricter traffic percent and monitoring.

Runbook: Canary rollback (operator steps):
1) From Redwood Console, navigate to Model > Deployments > Canary > <canary-id>.
2) Click "Pause traffic" to stop further expansion.
3) Execute rollback: 
   - CLI: rwctl deployment rollback --model rwinf-llama-2-70b --deployment <id> --artifact <prev-artifact>
   - Confirm that all quantized nodes are retired and replaced by the rollback artifact.
4) Verify metrics: latency.p95 and RSI have returned to baseline for 30 minutes.
5) If rollback fails or fallback policy triggers, open incident with priority P0.

A/B testing and long-term monitoring:
- For strategic launches, use A/B cohorts to compare cost/capability tradeoffs across identical slices. Sample size calculators are integrated into eval-mesh; default confidence target is 95%.
- Retain per-deployment perf-snapshot.json and eval reports for 90 days for forensic comparison.

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: Applied ML -> Quantization Team (owner alias: quant-team@redwood.ai)
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime -> Kernel and Scheduling (owner alias: runtime-kernels@redwood.ai)
- Oncall rotation: see eng-infra/oncall schedule.

Appendix: Useful CLI commands and diagnostic snippets:
- Collect quant metrics (10m window):
  curl -s "http://metrics-api.internal/collect?query=quant_quant_error_by_slice&window=10m&model=rwinf-llama-2-70b" | jq .
- Generate eval run locally (eval-harness):
  eval-harness run --model rwinf-llama-2-70b --quant-profile hybrid-kv-int4-fp16-attn --slices critical_user_queries --seeds 100 --output ./reports/q-eval.json
- Bisect command template:
  bisect-quant --model rwinf-llama-2-70b --artifact-list artifacts.txt --slices failing_slice --compare-to fp16-baseline --output bisect_report.json
